review_notes: Read the whole file and the sole downstream user (TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Coefficients/TwoDivisible.lean, lines 55-70), and checked Mathlib's ModuleCat.hom_smul simp lemma. I could not run Lean. My claims about how the simp discrimination tree treats the abbrev are inferences, not observations. The `htwo` duplication and the `simp↓` rationale are less certain, because I found no Mathlib `(2 : ZMod 2) = 0` simp lemma and did not check every simp-attribute convention.

findings.excerpt:
theorem modTwoCoefficientSequence_g_apply (z : ℤ) :
    modTwoCoefficientSequence.{u}.g (ULift.up z) = ULift.up (z : ZMod 2) := rfl
findings.problem: The only element-level simp lemma for `g` fires on the literal constructor form `ULift.up z`. The proofs in this file work with variable elements `a : ULift ℤ` (lines 62-74), so the lemma never applies there. Each proof instead unfolds `modTwoCoefficientSequence`, `AddEquiv.ulift` and `Equiv.ulift` by hand to compute `.down` of `g a`. The `simp↓` pre-lemma attribute is also unusual here. It only compensates for the lhs having to match before the `ULift.up` argument is rewritten, and it is not needed if the lemma is stated in `.down` form.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma on an arbitrary element in `.down` form, for example `(modTwoCoefficientSequence.{u}.g a).down = (a.down : ZMod 2)`, proved by `rfl` and tagged plain `@[simp]`. Keep the `ULift.up` version, if wanted, as a plain `@[simp]` lemma. Add the matching lemma `(modTwoCoefficientSequence.{u}.f a).down = 2 * a.down`. The exactness proof can then use `simp [htwo]` without unfolding `AddEquiv.ulift` or `Equiv.ulift`.
findings.benefit: Users and the file's own proofs get one canonical normal form for `.down` of `f` and `g` on arbitrary elements. They no longer need to unfold the implementation of the `ULift` additive equivalences, and `simp↓` is no longer needed.

findings.excerpt:
theorem modTwoCoefficientSequence_f :
    modTwoCoefficientSequence.{u}.f =
      (2 : ℤ) • 𝟙 (ModuleCat.of ℤ (ULift.{u} ℤ)) := rfl
findings.problem: `modTwoCoefficientSequence` is an `abbrev`, so it is reducible. `.f` applied to the `ShortComplex.mk` structure literal reduces by projection. The simp lemma's lhs can therefore be normalised to the same term as its rhs. Because the lemma is proved by `rfl`, it may be ineffective or have a degenerate key. This is an inference about discrimination-tree behaviour. I did not run Lean. The file's own proofs list `modTwoCoefficientSequence` explicitly in `simp [...]` calls (lines 66, 70, 74), as though this lemma did not do the work. Together with the abbrev, this makes the simp interface unclear. The sequence's `f` is stated in two ways, as a smul of `𝟙` and, via the missing element lemma, not at all.
findings.proposed_change: Decide on one mechanism. Either make `modTwoCoefficientSequence` a `def` with `@[simps]`-style or hand-written simp lemmas for `f`, `g`, `X₁`, `X₂` and `X₃`, so the simp normal form is controlled. Or keep the abbrev and drop the redundant `_f` simp attribute, replacing it with the element-level `.down` lemmas above. In both cases, remove the `modTwoCoefficientSequence` unfolding argument from the proofs' `simp` calls.
findings.benefit: This gives a predictable simp normal form for downstream code such as `simp [T, S, two_smul]` in TwoDivisible.lean, which maps `f` through a functor. It also avoids a simp lemma whose lhs and rhs coincide after reducible unfolding.

evidence.excerpt: @[simp] lemma hom_smul (s : S) (f : M ⟶ N) : (s • f).hom = s • f.hom := rfl

findings.problem: The fact `(2 : ZMod 2) = 0` is proved ad hoc as a local `htwo` here and again at line 69 in `modTwoCoefficientSequence_shortExact`, then passed to `simp` each time. There is no shared simp lemma for it. Each use of the sequence that needs `g ∘ f = 0` at the element level must rediscover the fact.
findings.proposed_change: Add one private or public lemma, for example `theorem two_eq_zero_zmod_two : (2 : ZMod 2) = 0 := by decide`, and use it in both places. Alternatively, state the element-level lemma `(g (f a)).down = 0` once and reuse it. Tag it `@[simp]` only if no existing Mathlib simp lemma already normalises this literal. I found none in Mathlib/Data/ZMod.
findings.benefit: This removes the duplicated local hypothesis and gives the simp calls a single named rule, so the simp set is explicit and consistent.
